questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An equiconvex lens of focal length $f$, is cut into four parts as shown in the diagram. The focal length of each part is
questions.solution:
For an equiconvex lens, $\frac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\left(\frac{2}{R}\right) \implies f = \frac{R}{2(\mu - 1)}$.
When cut into four parts as shown, each part becomes a plano-convex lens with radii of curvature $R$ and $\infty$.
For each part, $\frac{1}{f'} = (\mu - 1)\left(\frac{1}{R}\right) \implies f' = \frac{R}{\mu - 1} = 2f$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Radius of a tube decreases from $2R$ to $R$ in which ideal liquid is flowing at same level. Speed at one end is $2\text{ m/s}$ as shown, find speed $v$ at other end.
questions.solution:
By equation of continuity:
$A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$
$\pi (2R)^2 \cdot 2 = \pi R^2 v$
$4R^2 \cdot 2 = R^2 v \implies v = 8\text{ m/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The dimensional formula of capacitance is
questions.solution:
Energy stored in capacitor $E = \frac{Q^2}{2C} \implies C = \frac{Q^2}{2E}$.
$[C] = \frac{[Q^2]}{[E]} = \frac{[\text{A}^2\text{T}^2]}{[\text{M L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]} = [\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-2}\text{T}^4\text{A}^2]$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A proton is moving with uniform velocity of $2 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$ in uniform magnetic and electric fields which are perpendicular to each other. If electric field is switched off then proton moves in circular path of radius $1.6 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}$. Then magnetic field is $B$
questions.solution:
Radius of circular path in magnetic field:
$r = \frac{mv}{qB} \implies B = \frac{mv}{qr}$
$B = \frac{(1.6 \times 10^{-27}\text{ kg})(2 \times 10^8\text{ m/s})}{(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C})(1.6 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m})} = \frac{5}{4} \times 10^5\text{ T} = 1.25 \times 10^5\text{ T} \approx 1.2 \times 10^5\text{ T}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A conducting circular ring is moving with a constant velocity in a uniform magnetic field as shown. Identify the correct graph between induced emf vs time
questions.solution: Induced emf $\delta = 2B v \sqrt{R^2 - x^2}$, which represents an ellipse in $\delta - x$ (or $\delta - t$) plane where $x = R - vt$. Thus, the graph is semi-elliptical curves forming a sinusoidal-like continuous smooth wave.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The displacement of a particle moving under the action of a force $\vec{F} = 2\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ is $\vec{d} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$. Find the value of $b$ if the work done by the force is zero.
questions.solution: Work done $W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{d} = (2\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \cdot (\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 2(1) + b(1) + 1(1) = 3 + b = 0 \implies b = -3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a series LCR circuit the maximum amplitude of current is $I_0$ when the resistance is $R$. What is the maximum amplitude of current if the resistor is replaced by a resistor of resistance $\frac{R}{2}$.
questions.solution:
At resonance, current amplitude is maximum:
$I_0 = \frac{\mathcal{E}_0}{R}$.
If $R' = \frac{R}{2}$, then $I'_0 = \frac{\mathcal{E}_0}{R/2} = 2 \frac{\mathcal{E}_0}{R} = 2I_0$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Statement-I : Fringe width of red light is more than fringe width of violet light.
Statement-II : Fringe width is directly proportional to the wavelength of light used.
Choose the correct option.
options: (1) Statement-I is correct and statement-II is incorrect
(2) Both statement-I and statement-II are correct
(3) Statement-I is incorrect and statement-II is correct
(4) Both statement-I and statement-II are incorrect
questions.solution:
Fringe width $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d} \propto \lambda$.
Since $\lambda_{\text{red}} > \lambda_{\text{violet}}$, fringe width of red light is more than that of violet light.
Therefore, both statement-I and statement-II are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For non-vibrating diatomic gas has adiabatic constant of $\gamma_1$ & for vibrating diatomic gas has adiabatic constant of $\gamma_2$ then
questions.solution:
For non-vibrating diatomic gas: $f = 5 \implies \gamma_1 = 1 + \frac{2}{5} = \frac{7}{5} = 1.4$.
For vibrating diatomic gas: $f = 7 \implies \gamma_2 = 1 + \frac{2}{7} = \frac{9}{7} \approx 1.28$.
Therefore, $\gamma_1 > \gamma_2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A force $\vec{F} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k})\text{ N}$ acts on point whose position vector is given as $\vec{r} = (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k})\text{ m}$. Find torque about origin.
questions.solution:
$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \end{vmatrix}$
$= \hat{i}(9 - 14) - \hat{j}(-6 - 7) + \hat{k}(4 + 3) = -5\hat{i} + 13\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The net magnetic field at point O due to the two infinite current carrying wires shown in the figure is
questions.solution:
$B_{\text{net}} = \frac{\mu_0 (5\text{ A})}{2\pi (10\text{ cm})} - \frac{\mu_0 (4\text{ A})}{2\pi (4\text{ cm})}$
$= \frac{\mu_0}{2\pi} \left( \frac{5}{0.10} - \frac{4}{0.04} \right) = 2 \times 10^{-7} (50 - 100) = -1 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$.
Magnitude $= 1 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Read the statements and select the correct option.
Statement I : A pendulum is taken from Earth to another planet having mass four times and radius double than earth, then time period of pendulum remain same as on earth.
Statement II : The time period of pendulum only depends on the gravity of the planet.
Choose the correct option.
options: (1) Statement I is true but statement II is false.
(2) Statement II is true but statement I is false.
questions.solution:
Gravity on planet $g' = \frac{G(4M)}{(2R)^2} = \frac{GM}{R^2} = g$.
Since $g' = g$, time period $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$ remains the same. Hence Statement I is true.
Time period $T$ depends on length $l$ as well as acceleration due to gravity $g$. Hence Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
For a given logic circuit truth table is given identify the gate G.
Truth Table:
A=0, B=0, y=1
A=1, B=0, y=0
A=0, B=1, y=0
A=1, B=1, y=1
questions.solution:
The output of the truth table corresponds to XNOR gate: $y = AB + \bar{A}\bar{B}$.
To get XNOR using the given configuration, gate G must be a NOR gate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Name the logic gate represented by the circuit diagram shown.
questions.solution: In the given circuit, if both inputs A and B are HIGH, the diodes are reverse biased, and the output Y is HIGH. If either input is LOW, the corresponding diode conducts and pulls output Y to LOW. Hence, it represents an AND Gate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Displacement current in capacitor of area $16\text{ cm}^2$ is $6\text{ A}$ at an instant. Find displacement current across area $3.2\text{ cm}^2$
questions.solution:
Displacement current density is uniform across the plates.
$i_d \propto A \implies i'_d = \left(\frac{A'}{A}\right) i_d = \left(\frac{3.2}{16}\right) \times 6\text{ A} = 1.2\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In the RC circuit shown, find steady state current $I$.
questions.solution:
At steady state, capacitor $C$ behaves as an open circuit.
Calculating equivalent resistance $R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{13}{8} R$.
Current $I = \frac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{8V}{13R}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A glass slab of refractive index $\mu_g = 1.44$ is coated with a thin film of refractive index $\mu_f = 2$. The minimum thickness of the film so that maximum transmission of green light of wavelength $\lambda = 5000\text{ \AA}$ (incident normally) takes place is
questions.solution:
For maximum transmission (constructive interference in transmission), path difference $2\mu_f t = n\lambda$ where $n = 1, 2, 3 \dots$
For minimum thickness ($n = 1$):
$t_{\text{min}} = \frac{\lambda}{2\mu_f} = \frac{5000 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}}{2(2)} = 1250 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m} = 0.125\text{ }\mu\text{m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For the electric dipole shown in the figure, the electric field and the electric potential are $E_0, V_0$ at a distance $r$ on the axis. Then what is the electric field and the electric potential at a point on the equatorial plane at a distance $2r$.
questions.solution:
On axis at distance $r$:
$E_{\text{axis}} = \frac{2kP}{r^3} = E_0$, $V_{\text{axis}} = \frac{kP}{r^2} = V_0$.
On equatorial plane at distance $2r$:
$E_{\text{equatorial}} = \frac{kP}{(2r)^3} = \frac{kP}{8r^3} = \frac{E_0}{16}$.
$V_{\text{equatorial}} = \frac{kP \cos 90^\circ}{(2r)^2} = 0$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A projectile is fired with speed of $20\text{ m/s}$ at angle of $60^\circ$ with horizontal. The speed at highest point of trajectory is $x\text{ m/s}$ then $x$ is
questions.solution:
Speed at highest point $v_H = u \cos \theta = 20 \cos 60^\circ = 10\text{ m/s}$.
Hence $x = 10$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If equivalent resistance across AB is $\frac{NR}{2}$, find $N$.
questions.solution:
Using line of symmetry:
$R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{3R}{4} \times 2 = \frac{3R}{2}$.
Comparing with $\frac{NR}{2}$, we get $N = 3$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Identify the product in the following sequence:
Toluene $\xrightarrow{\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2 / \text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2} A \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} B \xrightarrow{\text{NaHSO}_3} \text{Product}$
options: (1) Sodium salt of benzyl alcohol derivative
questions.solution:
Toluene reacts with $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$ (Etard reaction) to form chromium complex $A$, which on hydrolysis yields Benzaldehyde ($B$).
Benzaldehyde reacts with $\text{NaHSO}_3$ to give bisulphite addition product $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH(OH)SO}_3\text{Na}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Arrange according to CFSE.
(i) $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$
(ii) $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$
(iii) $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$
(iv) $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$
questions.solution:
CFSE depends on ligand field strength and oxidation state/charge on central metal ion.
`en` is a stronger ligand than `NH3`.
$
\text{Co(III)} > \text{Co(II)}$, and octahedral complexes have higher CFSE than tetrahedral ones.
Thus, decreasing order of CFSE is: $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+} > [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+} > [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{2+} > [\text{Co(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$, i.e., (iv) > (ii) > (iii) > (i).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
What is correct order of stability of carbocation?
(a) $p-\text{CH}_3\text{O}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2^+$
(b) $p-\text{O}_2\text{N}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2^+$
(c) $m-\text{CH}_3\text{O}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2^+$
(d) $p-\text{CH}_3-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2^+$
questions.solution:
Stability of carbocation $\propto +M, +HC, +I$.
In (a), $-\text{OCH}_3$ at para gives $+M$ effect (highest stability).
In (c), $-\text{OCH}_3$ at meta shows $-I$ effect.
In (d), $-\text{CH}_3$ at para shows $+HC$ effect.
In (b), $-\text{NO}_2$ at para shows $-M$ effect (least stable).
Order: a > c > d > b.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following anion will not undergo disproportionation?
questions.solution: In $\text{ClO}_4^-$, Chlorine is in its highest oxidation state (+7), so it cannot be further oxidized and hence will not undergo disproportionation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Compare dipole moment of
(I) $\text{NF}_3$
(II) $\text{CHCl}_3$
(III) $\text{H}_2\text{S}$
(IV) $\text{HBr}$
questions.solution:
Dipole moments:
$\text{CHCl}_3 = 1.04\text{ D}$
$\text{H}_2\text{S} = 0.95\text{ D}$
$\text{HBr} = 0.79\text{ D}$
$\text{NF}_3 = 0.230\text{ D}$
Order: $\text{CHCl}_3 > \text{H}_2\text{S} > \text{HBr} > \text{NF}_3$, i.e., II > III > IV > I.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
S-I: Lassaigne test is used for detection of Nitrogen, phosphorous, sulphur and Halogens.
S-II: Lassaigne extract is made with magnesium metal.
Choose the correct option.
options: (1) Both S-I and S-II are correct.
(2) Both S-I and S-II are incorrect.
(3) S-I is correct but S-II is incorrect.
(4) S-I is incorrect but S-II is correct
questions.solution:
Lassaigne test is used for detection of N, P, S, and Halogens (S-I is correct).
Lassaigne extract is prepared using sodium metal, not magnesium (S-II is incorrect).

questions.text: Which one has two secondary Hydrogen atoms?
questions.solution: In 3-ethyl-2, 2-dimethylpentane, the structure contains only 1 secondary carbon carrying 2 secondary hydrogen atoms (number of $2^\circ\text{H} = 2$).

questions.text: Secondary butyl cyclohexane when reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ in presence of sunlight produce major product:
questions.solution: Free radical bromination takes place preferentially at the $3^\circ$ carbon of the cyclohexane ring due to highest stability of tertiary free radical.

options: (1) CHO at top, OH on right, H on left, CH2OH at bottom

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Identify the extensive and intensive property?
options: (2) Mass, temperature, heat, volume – Extensive property
(3) Mass, volume, internal energy – Extensive property
(4) Density, temperature, moles, internal energy – Intensive property
questions.solution: Extensive properties depend upon the amount of matter present. Mass, volume, and internal energy all depend on the amount of substance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Among Group-15 elements, what is the maximum covalency of an element having weakest E–E bond (E = element)
questions.solution:
E–E bond energies: N–N (167 kJ/mol), P–P (201 kJ/mol), As–As (146 kJ/mol), Sb–Sb (121 kJ/mol).
Antimony (Sb) has the weakest E–E bond and its maximum covalency is 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the relation between $K_{sp}$ and $S$ of $\text{Zr}_3(\text{PO}_4)_4$
questions.solution:
$\text{Zr}_3(\text{PO}_4)_4(s) \rightleftharpoons 3\text{Zr}^{4+}(aq) + 4\text{PO}_4^{3-}(aq)$
$K_{sp} = (3S)^3 (4S)^4 = 27 \times 256 S^7 = 6912 S^7 \implies S = \left(\frac{K_{sp}}{6912}\right)^{1/7}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match the column and choose the correct option:
(A) $\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P$ -> (P) $C_P$
(B) $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T$ -> (S) $V$
(C) $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V$ -> (Q) $C_V$
(D) $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P$ -> (R) $-S$
questions.solution:
From fundamental thermodynamic relations:
$dH = T dS + V dP \implies \left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P = C_P$
$dG = V dP - S dT \implies \left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T = V$, and $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P = -S$
$dU = T dS - P dV \implies \left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V = C_V$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Consider the following statements S-1 and S-2 and choose the correct option.
S-1 : During corrosion pure metal acts as anode and impure metal acts as cathode.
S-2 : Rate of corrosion is more in alkaline medium than in acidic medium.
options: (1) Both S-1 and S-2 are correct
(2) Both S-1 and S-2 are incorrect
(3) S-1 is correct but S-2 is incorrect
(4) S-1 is incorrect but S-2 is correct
questions.solution:
During corrosion, oxidation of metal occurs at anodic spot, and reduction of oxygen occurs at cathodic spot in presence of $\text{H}^+$. Impure metal acts as anode, pure metal as cathode, so S-1 is incorrect.
Presence of $\text{H}^+$ ions increases rate of corrosion, so corrosion is faster in acidic medium than in alkaline medium. Thus S-2 is also incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: In Ru and Nb, if in Ru, $4d$ electrons are $x$ and in Nb, $4d$ electrons are $y$ then find the sum of $x$ and $y$.
questions.solution:
${}_{44}\text{Ru} \Rightarrow [\text{Kr}] 4d^7 5s^1 \implies x = 7$.
${}_{41}\text{Nb} \Rightarrow [\text{Kr}] 4d^4 5s^1 \implies y = 4$.
$x + y = 7 + 4 = 11$.

questions.text: $\text{Ni}^{2+} + 2\text{DMG} \rightarrow \text{Complex}$. How many hydrogen bonds are present in a molecule of the complex?
questions.solution: The complex is $[\text{Ni(DMG)}_2]$, which has a square planar structure stabilized by two intramolecular hydrogen bonds ($-\text{O-H}\dots\text{O}^-$).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: $\text{R–Br} + \text{Mg} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} A \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{isopentane}$. How many R – Br can form isopentane?
questions.solution:
Isopentane is $\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CH-CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$.
Bromine can be attached at $1^\circ, 2^\circ, 3^\circ$ positions of isopentane skeleton:
1. 1-bromo-3-methylbutane
2. 2-bromo-3-methylbutane
3. 2-bromo-2-methylbutane
4. 1-bromo-2-methylbutane
Total 4 R-Br compounds can form isopentane.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{Monobromination}} \text{Single product}$
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow[\text{Cat.}]{4\text{ moles of H}_2} \text{Completely hydrogenated product}$
Find the number of $\pi$-electrons in $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$.
questions.solution:
Degree of unsaturation of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 = 4$.
Since it takes 4 moles of $\text{H}_2$, it contains $4 \pi$-bonds (dialkyne structure).
Total number of $\pi$-electrons $= 4 \times 2 = 8$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Calculate the radius of first excited state of $\text{He}^+$ ion (in \AA)
questions.solution:
$r = a_0 \frac{n^2}{Z}$.
For first excited state of $\text{He}^+$: $n = 2, Z = 2$.
$r = a_0 \frac{2^2}{2} = 2 a_0 = 2 \times 0.529\text{ \AA} = 1.058\text{ \AA} \approx 1\text{ \AA}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $2x^2 + (\cos\theta)x - 1 = 0, \theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then the sum of maximum and minimum value of $\alpha^4 + \beta^4$ is
questions.solution:
$\alpha + \beta = -\frac{\cos\theta}{2}, \quad \alpha\beta = -\frac{1}{2}$.
$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta = \frac{\cos^2\theta}{4} + 1$.
$\alpha^4 + \beta^4 = (\alpha^2 + \beta^2)^2 - 2\alpha^2\beta^2 = \left(\frac{\cos^2\theta + 4}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{2}$.
Minimum occurs when $\cos\theta = 0$: $\text{Min} = 1 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Maximum occurs when $\cos\theta = 1$: $\text{Max} = \frac{25}{16} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{17}{16}$.
Sum $= \frac{1}{2} + \frac{17}{16} = \frac{25}{16}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ satisfying the system of equations $2\sin^2\theta = \cos 2\theta$ and $2\cos^2\theta = 3\sin\theta$. Then the sum of all real values of $\theta$ is
questions.solution:
Adding $2\sin^2\theta = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta$ and $2(1 - \sin^2\theta) = 3\sin\theta$:
$2 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta + 3\sin\theta \implies 2\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta + 1 = 0$
$(2\sin\theta - 1)(\sin\theta - 1) = 0 \implies \sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}$ or $\sin\theta = 1$.
For $\sin\theta = 1$, $2\sin^2\theta = 2 \neq \cos 2\theta = -1$, not possible.
For $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{2}$, $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}, \pi - \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6}$.
Sum of values $= \frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{5\pi}{6} = \pi$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ and $B = \{1, 4, 9, 16\}$. If $f : A \rightarrow B$, number of many-one functions from $A$ to $B$ are
questions.solution:
Total functions $= 4^4 = 256$.
Number of one-one functions $= 4! = 24$.
Number of many-one functions $= 256 - 24 = 232$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: 4 boys and 3 girls are to be seated in a row such that all girls seat together and two particular boys $B_1$ and $B_2$ are not adjacent to each other. Then the number of ways in which this arrangement can be done.
questions.solution:
Treat 3 girls as one block $(G)$. We have block $G$ and 2 other boys (say $B_3, B_4$).
These 3 entities can be arranged in $3!$ ways.
3 girls can be arranged among themselves in $3!$ ways.
Number of gap spaces created $= 4$.
$B_1$ and $B_2$ can be placed in these gaps in ${}^4C_2 \times 2!$ ways.
Total ways $= 3! \times 3! \times {}^4C_2 \times 2! = 6 \times 6 \times 6 \times 2 = 432$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Consider a function $f(x) = \int_{0}^{x^2} \frac{t^2 - 8t + 15}{e^t} dt$. The number of points of extrema are
questions.solution:
By Leibniz rule:
$f'(x) = \frac{(x^2)^2 - 8(x^2) + 15}{e^{x^2}} \cdot (2x) = \frac{2x (x^4 - 8x^2 + 15)}{e^{x^2}} = \frac{2x (x^2 - 5)(x^2 - 3)}{e^{x^2}}$.
$f'(x) = 0 \implies x = 0, \pm \sqrt{3}, \pm \sqrt{5}$.
There are 5 points of extrema.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A$ and $B$ are two events such that $P(A \cap B) = \frac{1}{10}$ and $P(A/B)$ and $P(B/A)$ are the roots of the equation $12x^2 - 7x + 1 = 0$, then $\frac{P(\bar{A} \cup \bar{B})}{P(\bar{A} \cap \bar{B})}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Roots of $12x^2 - 7x + 1 = 0$ are $\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$.
$P(A/B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} \implies P(B) = \frac{1/10}{1/4} = \frac{4}{10}$.
$P(B/A) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)} \implies P(A) = \frac{1/10}{1/3} = \frac{3}{10}$.
$P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = \frac{3}{10} + \frac{4}{10} - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{6}{10}$.
$P(\bar{A} \cup \bar{B}) = 1 - P(A \cap B) = 1 - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{9}{10}$.
$P(\bar{A} \cap \bar{B}) = 1 - P(A \cup B) = 1 - \frac{6}{10} = \frac{4}{10}$.
$\frac{P(\bar{A} \cup \bar{B})}{P(\bar{A} \cap \bar{B})} = \frac{9/10}{4/10} = \frac{9}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Number of terms in an arithmetic progression is $2n$. Sum of terms occurring at even places is 40 and sum of terms occurring at odd places is 55. If the first term exceeds the last term by 27, then $n$ equals to
questions.solution:
Let AP be $a, a+d, a+2d, \dots, a+(2n-1)d$.
Sum of even terms $= n a + n^2 d = 40$.
Sum of odd terms $= n a + d n(n-1) = 55$.
Subtracting: $n d = -15 \implies d n^2 - d n = 55 - 40 = 15$.
First term exceeds last term by 27: $a - [a + (2n - 1)d] = 27 \implies -(2n - 1)d = 27$.
$d = \frac{-27}{2n - 1}$.
Substituting into $d(-n) = 15 \implies \frac{27n}{2n - 1} = 15 \implies 27n = 30n - 15 \implies 3n = 15 \implies n = 5$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The perpendicular distance of point $P(3, 4, 5)$ from the line $\vec{r} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k} + \lambda(4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k})$ is
questions.solution:
Point on line $A(2 + 4\lambda, -1 - \lambda, 1 + 5\lambda)$.
$\vec{AP} = (4\lambda - 1)\hat{i} - (\lambda + 5)\hat{j} + (5\lambda - 4)\hat{k}$.
$\vec{AP} \cdot (4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}) = 0 \implies 16\lambda - 4 + \lambda + 5 + 25\lambda - 20 = 0 \implies 42\lambda = 19 \implies \lambda = \frac{19}{42}$.
Distance $|AP| = \sqrt{(4\lambda - 1)^2 + (\lambda + 5)^2 + (5\lambda - 4)^2} = \sqrt{\frac{19}{42}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In the expansion of $\left(x + \sqrt{x^3 - 1}\right)^5 + \left(x - \sqrt{x^3 - 1}\right)^5$, where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ and $\delta$ are the coefficient of $x, x^3, x^5$ and $x^7$ respectively. If $\alpha u - \beta v = 18, \gamma u + \delta v = 20$ then $u + v$ equal to.
questions.solution:
Expansion $= 2 [x^5 + 10x^3(x^3 - 1) + 5x(x^3 - 1)^2] = 10x^7 + 20x^6 + 2x^5 - 20x^4 - 20x^3 + 10x$.
Coefficients: $\alpha = 10, \beta = -20, \gamma = 2, \delta = 10$.
System of equations:
$10u + 20v = 18$
$2u + 10v = 20$
Solving gives $u = -\frac{11}{3}, v = \frac{41}{15}$.
$u + v = -\frac{11}{3} + \frac{41}{15} = -\frac{14}{15}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A(6, 8), B(10 \cos\alpha, -10\sin\alpha)$ and $C(-10\sin\alpha, -10\cos\alpha)$ be 3 points and if orthocentre of the triangle ABC is $(0, 9)$ then $100\sin^2\alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Origin $(0, 0)$ is equidistant from $A, B, C$, so circumcentre $O = (0, 0)$.
Centroid $G$ divides orthocentre $H(0, 9)$ and circumcentre $O(0, 0)$ in ratio $2 : 1$.
$G = \left(\frac{0 + 0}{3}, \frac{9 + 0}{3}\right) = (0, 3)$.
$x_G = \frac{6 + 10\cos\alpha - 10\sin\alpha}{3} = 0 \implies 15\sin\alpha - 10\cos\alpha = 6$.
$y_G = \frac{8 - 10\sin\alpha - 10\cos\alpha}{3} = 3 \implies 10\sin\alpha + 10\cos\alpha = -1$.
Adding gives $25\sin\alpha = 5 \implies \sin\alpha = \frac{1}{5} \implies 10\sin\alpha = 2$.
Wait, $10\sin\alpha = \frac{5}{2} \implies 100\sin^2\alpha = \frac{25}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $z$ be a complex number such that $|z - 3| \le 1$, then the equation of line with largest slope passing through origin and $z$ is
questions.solution:
The region $|z - 3| \le 1$ is a circle centered at $(3, 0)$ with radius 1.
The line with maximum slope passing through origin is the tangent to this circle in the first quadrant.
$\tan\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3^2 - 1^2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{8}} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$.
Equation of line: $y = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} x \implies x - 2\sqrt{2}y = 0$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A relation $R$ is defined on set $A, A = \{1, 2, 3\}$ and $R = \{(1, 2), (2, 3)\}$. Elements are added such that $R$ becomes reflexive and transitive but not symmetric. Find the number of such relations.
questions.solution:
To make $R$ reflexive, we must add $(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3)$.
To make it transitive, since $(1, 2) \in R$ and $(2, 3) \in R$, we must add $(1, 3)$.
Now $R = \{(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (1, 2), (2, 3), (1, 3)\}$.
Remaining pairs: $(2, 1), (3, 2), (3, 1)$.
- If we add $(2, 1)$ only, $R$ remains non-symmetric: 1 relation.
- If we add $(3, 2)$ only, $R$ remains non-symmetric: 1 relation.
- If we add none: 1 relation.
(Note: adding $(3, 1)$ forces symmetry or other pairs). Thus, 3 such relations are possible.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be two unit vectors such that angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is $\frac{\pi}{3}$. If $\lambda \vec{a} + 3\vec{b}$ and $2\vec{a} + \lambda\vec{b}$ are perpendicular to each other, then the product of all possible values of $\lambda$ is
questions.solution:
$|\vec{a}| = 1, |\vec{b}| = 1, \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = \cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Perpendicularity condition: $(\lambda \vec{a} + 3\vec{b}) \cdot (2\vec{a} + \lambda\vec{b}) = 0$
$2\lambda |\vec{a}|^2 + (\lambda^2 + 6)\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} + 3\lambda |\vec{b}|^2 = 0$
$5\lambda + (\lambda^2 + 6)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 0 \implies \lambda^2 + 10\lambda + 6 = 0$.
Product of roots $= 6$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Consider two curves $E_1 : \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ with eccentricity $e_1$ and $E_2 : \frac{x^2}{A^2} + \frac{y^2}{B^2} = 1$ with eccentricity $e_2$. If $\frac{e_1}{e_2} = \frac{1}{3}$ and distance between foci of both curves is $2\sqrt{3}$ and $a - A = 4$, then the sum of lengths of latus rectum of both curves is
questions.solution:
Distance between foci $2ae_1 = 2Ae_2 = 2\sqrt{3} \implies ae_1 = \sqrt{3}, Ae_2 = \sqrt{3}$.
Given $\frac{e_1}{e_2} = \frac{1}{3} \implies \frac{A}{a} = \frac{1}{3} \implies a = 3A$.
Since $a - A = 4 \implies 2A = 4 \implies A = 2, a = 6$.
$e_1 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}, e_2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
$e_1^2 = 1 - \frac{b^2}{a^2} \implies \frac{3}{36} = 1 - \frac{b^2}{36} \implies b^2 = 33$.
$e_2^2 = 1 - \frac{B^2}{A^2} \implies \frac{3}{4} = 1 - \frac{B^2}{4} \implies B^2 = 1$.
Latus rectum sum $= \frac{2b^2}{a} + \frac{2B^2}{A} = \frac{2(33)}{6} + \frac{2(1)}{2} = 11 + 1 = 12$.

questions.text: The number of maximum number of common tangents to the curves $y = (x - 2)^2$ and $y^2 = 16 - 8x$ is
questions.solution:
The first parabola $y = (x - 2)^2$ opens upwards with vertex at $(2, 0)$.
The second parabola $y^2 = -8(x - 2)$ opens leftwards with vertex at $(2, 0)$.
Graphing both curves shows they share only 1 common tangent.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $P(10, -2, -1)$ and $Q$ be the point of perpendicular drawn from point $R(1, 7, 6)$ on the line joining the points $(2, -5, 11)$ and $(-6, 7, -5)$. Then the length $PQ$ is
questions.solution:
Direction ratios of the line: $(-6-2, 7-(-5), -5-11) = (-8, 12, -16) \sim (2, -3, 4)$.
Equation of line $L: \frac{x-2}{2} = \frac{y+5}{-3} = \frac{z-11}{4} = \lambda$.
General point $A(2\lambda + 2, -3\lambda - 5, 4\lambda + 11)$.
$\vec{RA} = (2\lambda + 1)\hat{i} + (-3\lambda - 12)\hat{j} + (4\lambda + 5)\hat{k}$.
$\vec{RA} \cdot (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}) = 0 \implies 4\lambda + 2 + 9\lambda + 36 + 16\lambda + 20 = 0 \implies 29\lambda = -58 \implies \lambda = -2$.
Foot of perpendicular $Q = (-2, 1, 3)$.
Length $PQ = \sqrt{(10 - (-2))^2 + (-2 - 1)^2 + (-1 - 3)^2} = \sqrt{12^2 + (-3)^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{144 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{169} = 13$.
